To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the lattice symmetry of the crystal imposes strong geometric constraints on its deformation.
the symmetry of the lattice induces a natural kinematical atlas on the strain space of 2D crystal elasticity, which is a key element in the understanding of the plasticity of 2D crystals.

(i) the lattice symmetry group induces a natural parameterisation of strain space, (ii) the lattice defects and their dynamics emerge naturally from the energy landscape, (iii) the energy landscape is the key to understanding the dynamics of the crystal, (iv) the symmetry group induces a rich structure in the energy landscape, which is the key to understand the dynamics of the lattice defects and of the crystal
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mathematical and numerical modelling of the mechanics of 2D crystals, with a particular focus on the role of lattice symmetry in the plastic flow.
the mathematical and numerical analysis of the geometric and topological properties of the energy landscape of a class of variational models of crystal plasticity.
the mathematical modelling and numerical simulation of the nonlinear dynamics of 2D crystal plasticity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the symmetry of the lattice is the main factor that determines the plastic behaviour of a crystal.
lattice symmetry is the key to understanding the plastic flow of crystals.
symmetry is the driving force behind all plastic phenomena in 2D crystals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the lattice symmetry is the key to understand the complex behaviour of crystals under mechanical loading.
the lattice symmetry determines the possible plastic mechanisms and the resulting defect-pattern complexity.
symmetry is a key ingredient for the understanding of the physics of plastic deformation in crystals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lattice symmetry group is a key element for understanding the plastic flow of crystalline materials.
the symmetry-induced kinematics and the underlying energy landscape are key to understanding the plastic flow and the defect-pattern formation.
the lattice symmetry group plays a fundamental role on the energy landscape, and thus on the dynamics and defect patterns induced by the minimization of a lattice invariant strain energy.
